transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Alex (Redwood SE), Priya (VertexAnalytics ML), Carlos (Infra), Marta (Product), Jules (DS)
---
[00:00] Samira: okay everyone thanks for hopping on, uh quick agenda — recap last week's runs, go over INT8 and FP8 numbers, quality examples, and decide next steps. Alex, do you want to start with the perf numbers?
[00:18] Alex: yeah sure, thanks Samira. um so quick note — these are the runs we pushed to the staging bucket yesterday, same model checkpoint, just different quantization flows. INT8 used static range quant, FP8 used the experimental block-fp8 path we discussed. throughput numbers first: INT8 measured about 1.8x tokens/sec vs baseline FP16 on our host infra, FP8 was around 2.3x. memory footprint dropped ~48% on INT8, ~62% on FP8. Latency p50: baseline 120ms, INT8 130ms (slightly up for small batches due to dequant cost), FP8 115ms. so FP8 actually improved p50 a bit.
[01:05] Priya: sorry can I clarify, you said INT8 latency went up? I thought quant usually reduces latency.
[01:12] Alex: yeah good call — depends on our kernel mix. for small batch sizes dequant and reformat overhead can dominate; the bigger wins show up in throughput for larger batches. for our 8-16 batch tests INT8 latency drops relative to fp16. the 130ms was a small-batch artifact, but p95s tell a different story, p95 INT8 is ~420ms vs 510ms baseline.
[01:42] Carlos: got it. what about infer cost delta? we need per-token cost estimates to compare.
[01:47] Samira: Alex, did you put the per-token cost in the spreadsheet?
[01:50] Alex: yup, included an estimated unit cost delta — INT8 roughly 35% cost reduction per token, FP8 around 50% on our infra assumptions (memory allows larger batch windows). spreadsheet link in chat.
[02:05] Marta: quick question on stability — any errors or divergence during longer sequences? we saw some hallucination upticks last time.
[02:12] Alex: good point. quality section: we ran the 2k holdout eval set (the prompt suite you shared). overall accuracy delta for INT8 was -0.9% absolute on classification tasks, FP8 was -0.3%. perplexity changes: INT8 +0.6pp, FP8 +0.2pp. so int8 shows a slightly larger quality hit, but not catastrophic. we also looked at per-example diffs and flagged 48 prompts where outputs diverged significantly with INT8.
[02:49] Priya: can you share examples of those divergent prompts? are they long-context or math-ish?
[02:55] Alex: mostly long-context summarization and a few numeric reasoning cases. i'll attach a sample of 10 diffs in the CSV. some are subtle wording changes, about 12 are more severe where ordering or facts flip.
[03:10] Jules: just to add — from our side, our eval pass includes ROUGE and an embedding-sim threshold; for INT8 a small percent drop in ROUGE, and about 2% more below-0.85 embedding-sim. those align with Alex's numbers.
[03:27] Samira: important tradeoff then: FP8 seems to give better perf and less quality degradation but is experimental on a few runtimes and may require special kernels / Dedicated cluster. Alex, status on FP8 readiness for Dedicated?
[03:38] Alex: FP8 is stable on our latest runtime build but requires enabling the FP8 compilation path; on Hosted we can run it as a gated experiment for you, but for sustained throughput at scale we recommend running on Dedicated GPUs with the FP8-enabled runtime — that avoids fallback to slower kernels. so it's doable, but we need to enable it in your test pool.
[03:58] Carlos: hmm ok. our security/compliance question — does enabling FP8 change anything re: determinism or audit logs? we need to keep reproducible outputs for some flows.
[04:08] Alex: FP8 can introduce tiny nondeterminism due to fused kernels and rounding, but from our tests variance is within normal nondeterminism of GPU ops. audit/logging is the same; KV cache behavior unchanged, it's just lower precision weights. we'll document the variance we observed.
[04:28] Priya: FYI some of our workflows require bit-for-bit reproducibility for debugging, that might be an issue. Are there options to run FP16 for those exact jobs?
[04:36] Samira: yes you can pin model variant per-route, run FP16 for those debug routes and use FP8 for high-volume endpoints. that's part of Redwood's routing options — can do per-route config.
[04:48] Marta: on the quality drop, what's the actionable path — more calibration, mixed-precision, or fine-tuning?
[04:55] Alex: we recommend a few approaches: 1) per-layer calibration for INT8 which can reduce the worst diffs (we saw 0.4% improvement after second calibration), 2) mixed-precision where attention uses FP16 and weights quantized, that brings accuracy close to baseline with some perf trade, 3) small delta fine-tune on 1-2k examples — that often recovers quality for sensitive prompts. we can help run the calibration pipeline.
[05:22] Priya: how long does calibration take? our infra windows are tight.
[05:26] Alex: for the 7B-ish model we used, the calibration pass on 2k calibration samples took ~45 minutes on a single GPU. FP8 path calibration is similar but slightly faster in practice.
[05:36] Carlos: ok provisioning reality — we can give you a 4x A100 test cluster for the week-of 8/17, but need exact config. Samira, can you outline what's needed from our infra folks?
[05:47] Samira: yes i'll send a short runbook. but short version: Dedicated test pool with FP8-enabled runtime, access to the staging model checkpoint S3 path, and IAM role to read the eval bucket. Alex will include the compile flags.
[06:02] Alex: also note the runtime does dynamic batching and KV cache — for summarization workloads we recommend batch window 8-16 to get best throughput without hurting latency SLO. i'll include suggested autoscale min/max.
[06:16] Jules: curious — did you try INT8 with activation clipping? that helped in some prior experiments.
[06:20] Alex: yes a couple runs with activation clipping and per-channel quant got the INT8 quality closer; delta reduced from -0.9% to -0.5%. there is a small perf hit though, around 1.1x vs 1.8x.
[06:36] Priya: what's the recommendation if we need strict quality on long-context docs? go FP8 or fine-tune?
[06:42] Alex: if strict quality is required, FP8 or mixed-precision plus a short fine-tune is safest. FP8 gave us only -0.3% absolute on your eval, so that seems promising.
[06:52] Marta: pricing question — Samira, can you summarize cost impact of Dedicated + FP8 license vs staying hosted fp16?
[06:58] Samira: yes — short take: raw infra cost per token goes down with FP8 by ~50% based on current runs, but there is an added licensing/ops uplift for Dedicated (we'll send a dedicated pricing line). net net for high volume endpoints FP8 on Dedicated is usually cheaper after you amortize reserved capacity. i'll send the numbers.
[07:16] Carlos: any risks re: vendor lock if we enable FP8-specific kernels?
[07:20] Samira: FP8 implementations use standard primitives and we'll provide the model artifacts. You're not locked to Redwood — the kernels are standard CUDA fused ops, but the compilation path is part of our runtime. we can export a model that runs in other runtimes but might need some engineering.
[07:35] Priya: ok next steps recap?
[07:37] Samira: Alex will share eval CSV + per-prompt diffs by Thursday 8/6. Priya will run extended 10k eval by 8/11 and share logs. Carlos will provision Dedicated test cluster by 8/13. Samira will send pricing. we'll reconvene after the 10k run for results and decide on a head-to-head benchmark week-of 8/17.
[07:58] Marta: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:01] Samira: thanks, i'll follow up in email with links to the spreadsheet and the runbook.
---
